\centering
    \begin{tabular}{|c|l|}
        \hline
        \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{{\bf Parameters in the Problem Formulation}}
        \\\hline
        ${\cal N}$ & The set of all items.
        \\\hline
        $n$ & The total number of items, and $n = |{\cal N}|$.
        \\\hline
        ${\cal D}$ & The unknown subset of defective items, distributed uniformly at random over all $\binom{n}{d}$ sets of size $d$.
        \\\hline
        $d$ & The number of defective items, with $d = |{\cal D}|$.
        \\\hline
        $f(\cdot)$ & The {\it test function}, a monotone function indicating the probability $f(x)$ that a test pool with $x$ defectives has a positive test outcome.
        \\\hline
        $\varepsilon$ & The pre-specified upper bound on the probability of incorrect reconstruction of ${\cal D}$.
        \\\hline
        $T$ & The number of tests.
        \\\hline
        
        \multicolumn{2}{c}{}
        \\\hline
     \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{{\bf Test Design and Decoding Parameters}}
        \\\hline
        ${\boldsymbol{M}}$ & The $T \times n$ binary test matrix: $M_{ji} = 1$ if item $i$ is in test $j$; $M_{ji} = 0$ otherwise.
        \\\hline
        ${q}$ & Probability with which each element in ${\boldsymbol{M}}$ is chosen as $1$ in an i.i.d. manner.
        \\\hline
        ${P(-,{q})}$ & The probability that a test containing $i$ has a positive outcome when $i$ is non-defective, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:p-p+}.
        \\\hline
        ${P(+,{q})}$ &  The probability that a test containing $i$ has a positive outcome when $i$ is defective, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:p-p+}.
        \\\hline
        ${Q(-,{q})}$ & The probability that a test excluding $i$ has a positive outcome when $i$ is non-defective, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:p-pp+p}.
        \\\hline
        ${Q(+,{q})}$ & The probability that a test excluding $i$ has a positive outcome when $i$ is defective, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:p-pp+p}.
        \\\hline
        ${\Delta({q})}$,${\nabla({q})}$ & The difference of test-positivity probability conditioned on item $i$ being defective or not, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:delta}.
        \\\hline
        ${P_{\min}({q})}$ & Minimal test sensitivity, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:Pmin}.
        \\\hline
        ${m}$, ${s}$ & Test participation parameter such that one item is included in $[{m},T-{s}]$ tests with high probability, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:m} and \eqref{eq:def:mo}.
        \\\hline
        ${{\Gamma}({q})}$ & The number of tests required in our algorithm, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:T}.
        \\\hline
        ${\hat{\Gamma}} ({q})$ & As defined in \eqref{eq:def:fTp}, an upper bound on ${{\Gamma}({q})}$ that is easier to analyze and optimize than ${{\Gamma}({q})}$.
        \\\hline
        ${{q}^*}$ & The parameter that minimizes ${\hat{\Gamma}} ({q})$, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:cpn} -- it can be efficiently approximated by Theorem \ref{thm:main}-\ref{thm1:item4}.
        \\\hline
        
        \multicolumn{2}{c}{}
        \\\hline
        
     \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{{\bf Parameters in the Achievability/Theorem \ref{thm:main}}}
        \\\hline
        ${H(f)}$ & The sensitivity parameter (as defined in \eqref{eq:def:sensi:para}) which helps bound $T$ from above in Theorem \ref{thm:main}-\ref{thm1:item3} and is bounded in Lemma \ref{lem:sensi:para:bound}.
        \\\hline
        ${\Gamma}_1({q})$& The number of tests required by Decoding Rule 1 in \eqref{eq:classification_small_q}, as defined in \eqref{eq:T_small_q}. 
        \\\hline
        ${\Gamma}_2({q})$ & The number of tests required by Decoding Rule 2 in \eqref{eq:classification_large_q}, as defined in \eqref{eq:T_large_q}. 
        \\\hline
        ${\hat{{q}}^*}$ & Any ${q}$ that is ``close enough" to ${{q}^*}$ -- the corresponding ${{\Gamma}({q})}$ can be bounded by $\Theta({\Gamma} ({{q}^*}))$ in Lemma \ref{lem:fT_error}.
        \\\hline
        ${\hat{{q}}}$ & An approximation to ${{q}^*}$. 
        \\\hline
        ${\alpha}$ & A useful parameter w.r.t. ${L}'$ and ${U}'$ in the saddle-point approximation in Lemma \ref{lem:int_U_L}, defined as $\frac{1}{2} \min\left\{{U}'-{L}',\sqrt{{L}'},\sqrt{d-{U}'}\right\}$. 
        \\\hline
        ${\beta}$ & The minimum term in ${H(f)}$ w.r.t. ${L}$ and ${U}$, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:beta}. 
        \\\hline
        

        \multicolumn{2}{c}{}
        \\\hline
     \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{{\bf Parameters in the Converse/Theorem \ref{thm:converse}}}
        \\\hline
        ${\chi}$ & The pool size. 
        \\\hline
        ${\mu}({\chi})$,${\sigma^{2}}({\chi})$ & The mean and variance of the test positivity probability, given that the pool size is ${\chi}$.
        \\\hline
        ${h(f)}$ & The concentration parameter (as defined in \eqref{eq:def:concen:para}) which helps bound $T$ from below in Theorem \ref{thm:converse}.
        \\\hline
        ${\chi}^*$ & The pool size that minimizes $({\mu}(1-{\mu}))/{\sigma^{2}}$, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:optimal-size}. 
        \\\hline
        $\boldsymbol{{X}}$ & The length-$n$ binary vector that is a weight $d$ vector representing the locations of the defective set ${\cal D}$.
        \\\hline
        $\boldsymbol{{Y}}$ &The length-$T$ binary vector representing the outcome of each test. 
        \\\hline
        $\boldsymbol{{Z}}$ &The length-$T$ vector representing the number of defectives in each test. 
        \\\hline
        $\boldsymbol{{\hat{X}}}$ & The length-$n$ binary vector representing the estimated locations of the defective set ${\cal D}$. 




        \\\hline
        
        
        \multicolumn{2}{c}{}
        \\\hline
     \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{{\bf Tightness Parameters/Theorem \ref{thm:match}}}
        \\\hline
        ${\vartheta}$ & The expected number of defectives in a test of pool size ${\chi}^*$, as defined in \eqref{eq:def:vartheta}.
        \\\hline
        $({\hat{L}},{\hat{U}})$ & A pair of parameters for ${H(f)}$ such that ${H(f)}$ is upper bounded by $\Theta(1/{\sigma^{2}}({\chi}^*))$.        
        \\\hline
        ${\eta}$ & The closest integer to ${\vartheta}$, as defined in \eqref{eq:match:def:eta}, which is one of the pair $({\hat{L}},{\hat{U}})$.
        \\\hline
        ${\kappa}$ & The other one of the pair $({\hat{L}},{\hat{U}})$, whose existence is proved in Lemma \ref{lem:match}.
        \\\hline

        \\\hline

nodes.statement: For test function , letting L=0 and U=1, we have from definition that H(f)leq 1.footnoteIndeed, we have H(f)=1 for this test function. The reverse inequality follows from . It then follows that the upper bound in scales as cal O left(dlog nright). On the other hand, recall from Remark that the lower bound in scales as Omegaleft(log binomndright). Indeed, we can show that the lower bound is precisely log binomnd, i.e., h(f)=1 for this test function. To see this, noting that f(0)=0 and f(a)=1, forall a geq 1, we can compute that mu(chi) = sumlimits_a=0^d fracbinomdabinomn-dchi-abinomnchi f(a) = 1 - fracbinomn-dchibinomnchi,\\ sumlimits_a=0^d fracbinomdabinomn-dchi-abinomnchi f^2(a) = 1 - fracbinomn-dchibinomnchi. Since (f(a) - mu(chi))^2=f^2(a) +mu^2(chi)-2f(a)mu(chi), we have from and that sigma^2(chi) &= sumlimits_a=0^d fracbinomdabinomn-dchi-abinomnchi (f(a) - mu(chi))^2\\ &= sumlimits_a=0^d fracbinomdabinomn-dchi-abinomnchi f^2(a) - mu^2(chi) \\ &= 1 - fracbinomn-dchibinomnchi - left( 1 - fracbinomn-dchibinomnchi right)^2 \\ &= fracbinomn-dchibinomnchi left( 1 - fracbinomn-dchibinomnchi right). It follows that fracmu(chi)(1-mu(chi))sigma^2(chi)=1, \; forall chiin \1,dots,n-1\. Thus we have h(f)=1 for this test function. Now the expression reduces to the classical Fano's inequality based information theoretic lower bound on the number of tests required for (1-varepsilon)-reliable recovery T geq frac1log eleft((1-varepsilon)logbinomnd - 1 right). By standard arguments via Stirling’s approximation, this quantity scales as Omegaleft(dlogfracndright). Finally, the assumption that d= n^theta,thetain(0,1) implies that our upper and lower bounds are order-wise tight, both scaling as Theta left(dlog nright).

\caption{Exact estimation of $d$}\label{algo:est}
    \begin{algorithmic}[1]
    \State $\textbf{Initialize } {\epsilon} \gets \frac{{\varepsilon}}{2\log n + 2}$, ${d_u} \gets 2$
    \While{true}
        \State $\textbf{set } {{\zeta}^*} = \mathrm{argmin}_{{\zeta}\in(0,1)} \frac{1-{\zeta}}{{\zeta} ({\Delta({d_u},{\zeta})})^2}$
        \State $\textbf{run } {\texttt{LoM}}({d_u},{{\zeta}^*},{\epsilon})$
        \State $\textbf{if } d \le {d_u}-1 \textbf{ then halt}$
        \State $\textbf{else set } {d_u} \gets 2{d_u}$
    \EndWhile
    \State $\textbf{set } {d_l} \gets \frac{{d_u}}{2}$

    \While{${d_u} - {d_l} \ge 2$}
        \State $\textbf{set } {d_m} = \left\lfloor \frac{{d_l}+{d_u}}{2} \right\rfloor \text{, } {{\zeta}^*} = \mathrm{argmin}_{{\zeta}\in(0,1)} \frac{1-{\zeta}}{{\zeta} ({\Delta({d_m},{\zeta})})^2}$
        \State $\textbf{run } {\texttt{LoM}}({d_m},{{\zeta}^*},{\epsilon})$
        \State $\textbf{if } d \le {d_m}-1 \textbf{ then set } {d_u} \gets {d_m}$
        \State $\textbf{else set } {d_l} \gets {d_m}$
    \EndWhile
    \State $\textbf{output } {d_l}$
    \end{algorithmic}
